cards.target: Trowch i dudalen deg.
cards.english: Turn to page ten.
cards.existing: Imperative ending `-wch` is formal/plural: `Eisteddwch` (sit down), `Cymerwch` (take), `Edrychwch` (look). Use this with `chi` (formal/group address).

cards.target: Mae heddiw'n well na ddoe.
cards.english: Today is better than yesterday.

cards.target: Mae heddiw'n oerach na ddoe.
cards.english: Today is colder than yesterday.

cards.target: Mae fy nhaid yn hoffi garddio.
cards.english: My grandfather likes gardening.

cards.target: Mae'r terfyn cyflymder yn dri deg.
cards.english: The speed limit is thirty.

cards.target: Mae'r llong yn gadael am chwech.
cards.english: The ship leaves at six.

cards.target: Mae fy mhlant yn tyfu'n gyflym.
cards.english: My children are growing fast.
cards.existing: Nasal mutation makes voiced stops nasal: b→m, d→n, g→ng. Hardest to spot – the consonant looks like a different letter.

cards.target: Mae fy nghefnder yn ddeg oed.
cards.english: My cousin is ten years old.
cards.existing: Nasal mutation after fy (my) and yn (in): p→mh, t→nh, c→ngh, b→m, d→n, g→ng. Pen → fy mhen (my head). Caerdydd → yng Nghaerdydd.

cards.target: Mae'r swyddfa ar y trydydd llawr.
cards.english: The office is on the third floor.

cards.target: Dyw e ddim cystal â'r llall.
cards.english: It's not as good as the other.
cards.existing: Negation in Welsh: insert `ddim` after the subject. `Dw i'n hapus` (I'm happy) → `dw i ddim yn hapus` (I'm not happy). Notice `yn` stays for adjectives.

cards.target: Mae fy mam-gu yn byw yng Ngheredigion.
cards.english: My grandmother lives in Ceredigion.

cards.target: Mae fy mam-gu yn byw gyda ni.
cards.english: My grandmother lives with us.

cards.target: Mae fy mrawd bach yn bedair oed.
cards.english: My little brother is four.

cards.target: Dim ond bore ddoe wnes i glywed.
cards.english: It was only yesterday morning that I heard.
cards.existing: `Dim ond` = 'only / just': `Dim ond te, diolch` (Just tea, thanks). Literally 'nothing but'. Restrictive.

cards.target: Dydyn ni ddim eisiau bod yn hwyr.
cards.english: We don't want to be late.
cards.existing: Some verbs negate by changing form: `dw → dwy(t)`, `mae → dyw/dydy`. You'll see different shapes for the same root depending on positive/negative/question.

cards.target: Does dim siwgr yn y te yma.
cards.english: There's no sugar in this tea.
cards.existing: Formal/written: `Nid oes` instead of `does`. `Nid oes neb yma` (there's nobody here). Same meaning, different register.

cards.target: Mae ei mam yn gweithio yn yr ysgol.
cards.english: Her mother works at the school.

cards.target: Mae'n ddrwg gen i, dw i ddim yn deall.
cards.english: I'm sorry, I don't understand.

cards.target: Dyw dy ymdrech ddim wedi mynd heb ei sylwi.
cards.english: Your effort hasn't gone unnoticed.

cards.target: Dyn ni wedi bod yn briod ers ugain mlynedd.
cards.english: We've been married for twenty years.

cards.target: Mae ei llais hi'n cario ar draws yr ystafell.
cards.english: Her voice carries across the room.

cards.target: Dw i ddim wedi darllen y llyfr yna eto.
cards.english: I haven't read that book yet.

cards.target: Mae fy mhlant yn caru chwarae yn yr ardd.
cards.english: My children love playing in the garden.

cards.target: Dw i'n colli fy nheulu pan dw i i ffwrdd.
cards.english: I miss my family when I'm away.

cards.target: Mae pedwar math o gynghanedd.
cards.english: There are four types of cynghanedd.

cards.target: Mae pedwar tymor mewn blwyddyn.
cards.english: There are four seasons in a year.

cards.target: Mae ei gwên hi'n goleuo'r ystafell.
cards.english: Her smile lights up the room.

cards.target: Mae pum afal yn y bowlen.
cards.english: There are five apples in the bowl.

cards.target: Mae fy nheulu'n wreiddiol o'r Cymoedd.
cards.english: My family is originally from the Valleys.

cards.target: Mae fy ewythr yn blismon wedi ymddeol.
cards.english: My uncle is a retired police officer.

cards.target: Mae fy mhlant yn yr ysgol feithrin.
cards.english: My children are in nursery school.

cards.target: Mae eu plant nhw'n mynychu'r ysgol leol.
cards.english: Their children attend the local school.

cards.target: Dw i'n reidio fy meic i'r orsaf.
cards.english: I ride my bike to the station.

cards.target: Bydda i'n ymarfer fy Nghymraeg bob nos.
cards.english: I will practise my Welsh every evening.

cards.target: Mae fy nith eisiau bod yn filfeddyg.
cards.english: My niece wants to be a vet.

cards.target: Mae ei goginio e'n gwella bob wythnos.
cards.english: His cooking is getting better every week.

cards.target: Mae ei dealltwriaeth o'r iaith yn drawiadol.
cards.english: Her understanding of the language is impressive.

cards.target: Mae eu tŷ nhw'n edrych dros y dyffryn.
cards.english: Their house overlooks the valley.

cards.target: Mae fy ffrind gorau yn byw yn Abertawe.
cards.english: My best friend lives in Swansea.

cards.target: Mae fy merch yn astudio yn y brifysgol.
cards.english: My daughter is studying at university.

cards.target: Mae ein capel ni'n cynnal gwasanaethau bob Sul.
cards.english: Our chapel holds services every Sunday.

cards.target: Mae e'n helpu ei rieni ar y penwythnos.
cards.english: He helps his parents at the weekend.

cards.target: Dw i'n agos iawn at fy nghefnder Hywel.
cards.english: I'm very close to my cousin Hywel.

cards.target: Mae ei deulu wedi byw yma ers cenedlaethau.
cards.english: His family has lived here for generations.

cards.target: Mae fy nai'n chwarae i'r tîm pêl-droed lleol.
cards.english: My nephew plays for the local football team.

cards.target: Mae'r trên stêm yn teithio drwy'r bwlch mynyddig.
cards.english: The steam train travels through the mountain pass.

cards.target: Mae'r daith yr un mor bwysig â'r cyrchfan.
cards.english: The journey is just as important as the destination.

cards.target: Mae fy mam yn coginio cawl bob dydd Sul.
cards.english: My mum cooks cawl every Sunday.

cards.target: Mae tri deg wyth o ddisgyblion yn y dosbarth.
cards.english: There are thirty-eight pupils in the class.

cards.target: Mae'r geiriadur yn cynnwys dros ddeg mil o eiriau.
cards.english: The dictionary contains over ten thousand words.

cards.target: Mae'r cyngerdd ar y pedwerydd ar bymtheg o Orffennaf.
cards.english: The concert is on the nineteenth of July.

cards.target: Bydda i'n coginio rhywbeth arbennig ar gyfer dy ben-blwydd.
cards.english: I will cook something special for your birthday.

cards.target: Mae hi'n debyg i'w mam o ran ei gwên.
cards.english: She's similar to her mother in the way she smiles.

cards.target: Mae pedwar cant a hanner o filltiroedd i Lundain.
cards.english: It is four hundred and fifty miles to London.

cards.target: Dw i'n anfon llythyr at fy ffrind yng Nghaerdydd.
cards.english: I'm sending a letter to my friend in Cardiff.

cards.target: Does dim amser gyda ni i gwblhau'r gwaith heddiw.
cards.english: We have no time to complete the work today.
cards.existing: Formal/written: `Nid oes` instead of `does`. `Nid oes neb yma` (there's nobody here). Same meaning, different register.

cards.target: Dyw'r cawl ddim mor boeth ag oeddwn i'n disgwyl.
cards.english: The soup is not as hot as I expected.

cards.target: Fy enw i ydy Dafydd, a dw i'n dysgu Cymraeg.
cards.english: My name is Dafydd and I'm learning Welsh.

cards.target: Mae fy nai yn dysgu Cymraeg yn yr ysgol feithrin.
cards.english: My nephew is learning Welsh at nursery school.

cards.target: Mae fy mrawd yn smwddio'i grys ar gyfer y gwaith.
cards.english: My brother is ironing his shirt for work.

cards.target: Mae Dydd Santes Dwynwen ar y pumed ar hugain o Ionawr.
cards.english: St Dwynwen's Day is on the twenty-fifth of January.

cards.target: Nid yn unig mae hi'n siarad Cymraeg, ond mae hi hefyd yn siarad Gwyddeleg.
cards.english: Not only does she speak Welsh, but she also speaks Irish.

cards.target: Mewn gwirionedd, does dim problem cyn belled â bod pawb yn dilyn y rheolau cytunedig.
cards.english: In reality, there is no problem as long as everyone follows the agreed rules.
cards.existing: Pair with `gen/gyda` for possession: `Does dim car gen i` (I don't have a car). The negation structure stays – only the prepositional phrase changes.

cards.target: Mae'r pentathlon yn cyfuno pum camp wahanol.
cards.english: The pentathlon combines five different disciplines.

cards.target: Casglоdd y ddeiseb ddeng mil o lofnodion.
cards.english: The petition gathered ten thousand signatures.
cards.existing: Welsh nouns have two genders: masculine and feminine. There's no neutral or 'thing' category – every noun is one or the other, arbitrarily. `Cath` (cat) is feminine; `ci` (dog) is masculine.

cards.target: Mae'r llysgennad yn cynrychioli ei wlad dramor.
cards.english: The ambassador represents his country abroad.

cards.target: Casglоdd e naw stamp o wahanol wledydd.
cards.english: He collected nine stamps from different countries.

cards.target: Mae'r rhestr fer yn cynnwys pump o ymgeiswyr.
cards.english: The shortlist includes five candidates.

cards.target: Sefydlwyd y cwmni ym mil naw wyth pump.
cards.english: The company was established in 1985.

cards.target: Mae'r tŵr yn saith deg metr o uchder.
cards.english: The tower is seventy metres in height.

cards.target: Mae dau gi a dwy gath gyda ni.
cards.english: We have two dogs and two cats.

cards.target: Mae'r walts yn ddawns osgeiddig mewn tri amser.
cards.english: The waltz is a graceful dance in triple time.

cards.target: Mae'r gomed yn ymddangos bob saith deg pump mlynedd.
cards.english: The comet appears every seventy-five years.

cards.target: Mae'r nitrogen yn ffurfio wyth deg y cant o'r atmosffer.
cards.english: Nitrogen forms eighty percent of the atmosphere.

cards.target: Rhaid i'r traethawd hir fod yn o leiaf deg mil o eiriau.
cards.english: The dissertation must be at least ten thousand words.
cards.existing: `Rhaid i + person + verb-noun` = 'must / has to'. `Rhaid i fi fynd` = 'I must go'. Literal: 'necessity to me to go'. Welsh frames obligation as a state of necessity.
